tool.name: GAPPA graft
tool.description: place query sequences as leaves on a reference tree
tool.command: ln -s '$jplace' placements.jplace && gappa examine graft --jplace-path placements.jplace --threads "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" $fully_resolve

param.label: Resolve each query as an individual branch
param.help: Disabled: queries on one reference branch are collected in a subtree. Enabled: place each query using its individual distal/proximal length.

tool.help:
Add placed query sequences as leaves to the reference phylogeny stored in a **jplace JSON** dataset from EPA-ng or pplacer.
The result is a Newick tree containing reference and query leaf names. GAPPA selects the most likely placement for each query, so the tree presents one position per query even when the input retains multiple candidate placements. Keep the original jplace data when interpreting placement uncertainty.
By default, queries placed on the same reference edge are grouped in a subtree attached to that edge. Enable **fully resolve** to insert queries individually at their placement positions along the edge. This changes the displayed topology; it does not estimate a new reference phylogeny, realign sequences or recalculate placement likelihoods.
Use the Newick output for downstream tree analysis or visualization. Query and reference identifiers are retained for joining with abundance or annotation tables.
